steps.note: S2.3.4b states that rows 0-1 subtract Ja+Rc, rows 2-5 add J(a+Vx)+R(c+Gx) and rows 6-7 restore a,c, so the net change (JV+RG)x is independent of a,c, quoting line 744.
S2.3.4c gives the bit-case central coefficient |S∩T| mod 2, the side injection cancelling exactly the intersection-one cases, and self coefficient one.
S2.3.4d gives the complex central coefficient (|S∩T|-1)/2, side cancellation for intersections zero and two, zero for intersection one, and self coefficient one.
S2.3.5 states the forward/inverse/forward stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) restoring every auxiliary value, with S2.3.1 giving each invocation its own scratch wires.
S2.5.5b quotes the full residual table with every edge's orthogonal residual and dimension, and S2.5.5a states that every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels.
S2.5.5d states that t_X ⊥ t_Y gives <t_X> ⊂ t_Y^⊥ and that the complement <t_X,t_Y>^⊥ has dimension h-2.
The plan states that the only decreasing edge is center 3->4 with loss h, and that gate telescoping gives sources N, sinks Wm-N, signed sum Wm-2N and absolute sum Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich.
S2.5.5f states that each nonzero binary residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating and so has an orthonormal basis, and its quote includes the absorption of alternating planes via w+a, w+b, w+a+b.
S2.5.5g gives L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 exactly.
S2.6.5 gives the weight formula and additivity mod 4 for orthogonal vectors, and S2.6.6 gives q_V-q_U as the sum of wt(v)[v·x] over an orthonormal residual basis.
S2.6.7 states that wt(v) is odd so the phase is i^{ε[v·x]}, and that H diag(1,-1) H = X turns it into aI+bX_v or its inverse.
S2.6.9 states that on k columns each residual vector contributes one factor K_{e,v}^{⊗k}, giving s_c factors over the network.

The plan gives frame I for the zero label and C^{⊗m} for the full label, C^{-1} on the 27 support coordinates for X_a->Y_a, the repair by Z_{a,k} before and i^{27k}Z_{a,k} after using C=iZC^{-1}Z, and negation of the X outputs.
The plan states that both loss ratios are below 1/2, which gives deficits N-2L_b>0 and 2N-2L_c>0, with s_b<W_b m and s_c<W_c m.
The plan states that both deficits exceed 20·2^{-50} and log m<20, so m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-η), which gives s/W<m^τ with τ=σ=1-2^{-50}.
S2.8.2-S2.8.3 give the pivot at the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, clearing by lower-triangular elementary operations, repetition on the active indices, and exactly a ones in Π.

S2.8.4 only asserts that a fixed odd prime q exists; the plan never says the prime avoids the denominators of a finite table of factors so that the identities specialize to Z/q^b with invertible triangular factors (S2.5.6b and S2.9.2 mention coprime radices and denominators only in other roles).
S2.8.5 states that a lower-triangular transformation costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order with a diagonal unit and earlier coordinates.
S2.8.6-S2.8.8 give each one of Π as H_i<-H_i+D_j, realized by D_j<-D_j+H_i, an interchange and D_j<-H_i-D_j, with one interchange each and a in all.
S2.12.8c gives A(e)≤sA(e/m)+E at internal nodes and A(e)≤8e at leaves, and S2.12.8b bounds the per-invocation count by 24W^3+4s+4W+4<E.
S2.12.8d gives B^{k+1}≤B^2 d^ν and A(e)≤8B^2 d^{ν+1}, and S2.12.8e gives a total below 128mB^2 d^{ν+3}≤C_0 d^{C_1}.
S2.12.8f states that depth-ℓ values lie in 2^{-(p+ℓ)}Z[i] with modulus at most 2^ℓ and that p+Δ fractional plus Δ+3 integer bits are exact, and S2.12.8g states that εC_1<1 gives Δ=o(p).
S2.12.10e states that every row of the butterfly matrix has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved and truncation errs by less than √2·2^{-p}.

summary: P01 quotes nearly every cited derivation in place: the bank-exchange proof, the residual table and its telescoping, the phase-frame interface, the exact deficits, the shear elimination and the depth/growth bounds of the layer. The one omission is M2: the plan asserts that a fixed odd prime exists for the matrix shear but never gives the reason, namely avoiding the denominators of a finite table of factors so that the identities specialize to Z/q^b with invertible triangular factors. 25 of 26 present.
